title: Getting Started Again
eyebrow: Proposal from the friction audit · pick where to start · nothing built yet

short.lead: The audit found that Focus Deck was built and tested with 66 tasks. With 400 or more tasks across 26 projects, every screen turns back into the wall of choices the app exists to remove. Before you can start one task, you choose from 64 cards on the Focus screen. On a phone that means swiping through two carousels one card at a time. On desktop it means about three screens of scrolling. Your GitHub workflow labels, like Needs review and Duplicate, also show up as kinds of work. Below are four directions. Each one is a design proposal first, with no code until you approve it.
short.hint: Tap each row to see what it changes. The first two have pictures from the real app loaded at your size.
items: Focus asks for a project (1 of 27) and then a label (1 of 37), one swipe per card, with no search. A project in the middle of the list is about 13 swipes away.

items.alt: Phone Focus screen showing project carousel 1 of 27 and label carousel 1 of 37
items.caption: Today on a phone, with 420 tasks.

items: 64 cards, Surprise me at the bottom
27 folders and 37 label cards fill about three screens. Most folders say 'top: Urgent', so that line stops meaning anything. Labels like Duplicate and AjsAgent created this appear as kinds of work.

items.alt: Desktop Focus screen, full length, with 27 project folders and 37 label cards
items.caption: Today on desktop, the whole page.

items: Focus opens on three suggested tasks, ranked by due date, priority and what is already in progress, with 'Pick one for me' at the top. The folders and labels move behind one 'Narrow it down' button. It works the same way on a phone and on desktop. This is the biggest change.
Decide if this is where you want to end up.

Workflow labels (Needs review, Duplicate, Wontfix, AjsAgent created this and similar) stop showing as kinds of work. Asap and highest priority count as priority. In Settings you tick, once, which labels are kinds of work. The label list on Focus drops from 37 cards to the ones you tick. This is small, and it makes the suggestions in A trustworthy. It is my suggestion for the first build.

Sort the thoughts for one project together, pick a project from a searchable list instead of a carousel on a phone, and put the main button within thumb reach. With 44 thoughts waiting, this cuts the steps per thought.
Decide if sorting is your biggest pain.

There are 97 open issues. 15 are built and waiting for your review, the old Board issues #140 to #147 are still open after the Board was replaced, and Bursts A to G overlap the issues they group. I would make a list of what to close and which urgency labels to merge, for you to approve. Nothing is closed without your yes. Issue #162 already asks for this.
Decide if I make that list.

changes: B shortens the label list. A replaces the two pickers with three suggestions.
Your GitHub labels stay on GitHub as they are. Only what Focus Deck shows changes.
The three sorting steps stay. C changes how many thoughts you sort at once and how you pick the project.
The audit found problems there too (the Board ignores priority, and project cards show up to four labels per task). They come after you pick a start.
Nothing is deleted. GitHub and Gist sync work as today.
choices: The biggest gain for starting tasks, but the biggest build, and its suggestions lean on clean priority labels.
Small, quick to feel, and it shrinks the Focus screen right away. A can follow straight after.
Best if the 44 thoughts in Sort are what stops you most.
I suggest B because it is small, you would feel it within a day, and it makes A's suggestions trustworthy.
Should I tidy the Focus Deck issue backlog too?
Yes, make a list for me to approve
I list what to close and which labels to merge. Nothing changes on GitHub until you say yes.
The backlog stays as it is, and we only work on the app.
I suggest Yes because 97 open issues make it hard for you to see what is actually left.

wrapup.summary: The audit's fix is to make starting a task take one tap again. My suggestions are to clean up labels and priority first, and to have me make a backlog list for you to approve.
wrapup.changing: Changed: only the parts of the app named by the direction you pick. Kept: your data, sync, and every screen the direction doesn't touch.
wrapup.blocking: Waiting on your answers to the two questions in Choices. Nothing is built until you approve.
wrapup.next: After you approve, I will draw the design for your pick on the real screens, at phone and desktop size, for you to approve before any code.
